column5: Gripping the blade in one hand, he uses the other to punch me.{w}\nRepeatedly in my chest, causing the wound to open more, and bleed.{w}\nI kick and scream in agony, trying my best to withstand his harsh blows.
column6: 他一手紧握刀刃，另一只手挥拳砸向我。{w}\n一拳又一拳落在我的胸口，让伤口裂得更开，鲜血直流。{w}\n我在剧痛中又踢又叫，竭力承受着他凶狠的殴打。

column5: He's smart. Soon enough, the pain is too much to fight back.{w}\nI can only squirm and wince underneath him, enduring the assault.{w}\nThe cavern starts to crumble, and pieces fall from the ceiling.
column6: 他很聪明。很快，剧痛就让我再也无力反抗。{w}\n我只能在他身下扭动、皱眉，默默忍受着这顿殴打。{w}\n洞窟开始崩塌，碎石从洞顶纷纷落下。

column5: There's no one here to save you, [firstname].\nYour life is mine, and The Rebellion is no more.
column6: 这里没有人会来救你，[firstname]。\n你的命属于我，而反抗军已不复存在。

column5: There's no one here to save you, [firstname].\nYour life is mine, and The Rebellion is no more.
column6: 这里没有人会来救你，[firstname]。\n你的命属于我，而反抗军已不复存在。

column5: Smirking, he lowers the blade to my neck.
column6: 他冷笑着，把刀刃向下抵到我的脖子上。

column5: May The Triumvirate reign eternal.
column6: 愿三人执政团永世长存。

column5: I use all of my strength to reach up, and grab the blade.{w}\nTrying to push it away, I realize there's almost no point.{w}\nBut soon after, the blade reacts to both of our touches.
column6: 我用尽全力抬手，抓住了刀刃。{w}\n我试图把它推开，却发现几乎毫无用处。{w}\n但没过多久，刀刃对我和他的触碰都起了反应。

column5: Another flash of white light engulfs the entire room.{w}\nThe pressure is relieved from my neck, and I hear Sovy struggle.{w}\nJust like Gryz said — the blade reacts to the will of the wielder.
column6: 又一道白光吞没了整个房间。{w}\n我脖子上的压迫感松开了，我听见索维在挣扎。{w}\n正如格瑞兹所说——刀刃会回应持刀者的意志。

column5: But whose will was stronger...?
column6: 但究竟谁的意志更强……？

column5: I raise up my other hand to grab the blade as well.{w}\nI close my eyes, and focus with every fiber of my being.{w}\nSpirits — please do something! Save me! Save us all...!
column6: 我抬起另一只手，也抓住了刀刃。{w}\n我闭上眼，倾尽身心全部的力量专注起来。{w}\n灵啊——求你们做点什么！救救我！救救我们所有人……！

column5: The light subsides, and I see Sovy looking down at me in shock.{w}\nI can see the horror in his eyes, but I have no idea what just happened.{w}\nPerhaps the blade gave him visions, like it did for me back in Valinorth.
column6: 光芒褪去，我看见索维惊骇地俯视着我。{w}\n我能从他眼中看到恐惧，却完全不知道刚才发生了什么。{w}\n也许那刀刃也让他看见了幻象，就像当初在瓦利诺斯对我那样。

column5: He panics and throws the blade on the ground.
column6: 他惊慌失措，把刀刃扔到了地上。

column5: So it {i}is{/i} true...\nThe Spirit Realm is—
column6: 看来那{i}的确{/i}是真的……\n灵界竟然——

column5: Slowly standing up, he takes a few steps back.{w}\nLooking down in my eyes, I can see sadness within him.{w}\nSo many conflicting emotions, all in the span of a few seconds.
column6: 他缓缓站起，向后退了几步。{w}\n他俯视着我的眼睛，我能看出他内心的悲伤。{w}\n那么多相互冲突的情绪，全都挤在短短几秒之内。

column5: He scoffs, and turns his back to me.
column6: 他嗤笑一声，转过身背对着我。

column5: Remember my mercy, Seer...\nNext time, you won't be so lucky.
column6: 记住我的仁慈，先知……\n下一次，你可就不会这么走运了。

column5: Remember my mercy, Seeress.\nNext time, you won't be so lucky.
column6: 记住我的仁慈，先知……\n下一次，你可就不会这么走运了。

column5: To my complete shock, he simply runs away.{w}\nI tilt my head to the side, and watch him leave.{w}\nThe blade rests beside me, so I reach for it.
column6: 让我完全没想到的是，他就那样转身逃走了。{w}\n我侧过头，看着他离去。{w}\n刀刃就落在我身旁，于是我伸手去够。

column5: But any hope of salvation is quickly lost. It's over...{w}\nAs soon as Sovy leaves the room, it starts to cave in.{w}\nRubble and debris block the exit, leaving me trapped inside.
column6: 但得救的希望很快就破灭了。一切都结束了……{w}\n索维一离开房间，这里就开始塌陷。{w}\n碎石瓦砾堵住了出口，把我困在了里面。

column5: I look over at Damek's lifeless body, and start to cry.{w}\nMy wound bleeds profusely, and my vision slowly wanes.{w}\nWith my final moments, I grip the blade, and pray for help.
column6: 我望向达梅克毫无生气的尸体，哭了起来。{w}\n我的伤口大量失血，视野渐渐模糊。{w}\n在最后的时刻，我握紧刀刃，祈祷有人来救我。

column5: But before I slip away into nothingness, that help never comes.
column6: 但在我坠入虚无之前，那份救助始终没有到来。

column5: Ulric and Pro stand back to back, destroying the Honor Guard with ease.{w}\nThe pirates, on the other hand, keep Shane and Halin occupied.{w}\nThey were starting to come back from this. They could survive.
column6: 乌尔里克和普洛背靠背站立，轻松地击溃着荣誉卫队。{w}\n另一边，海盗们缠住了肖恩和哈林。{w}\n他们正逐渐扭转局势。他们能活下来。

column5: Another one down...!\nCome on Ulric, pick up the pace.\nIf you lose this, you'll never hear the end of it.
column6: 又一个倒下了……！\n来吧乌尔里克，加快点速度。\n要是你输了这场，我可会一直念叨到你别想消停。

column5: Ulric takes down four suits of armor with one swing of his sword.
column6: 乌尔里克一剑挥出，击倒了四副铠甲。

column5: Oh, we're keeping count...?\nThen I think Alex and his crew are winning.\nBut at least now we know who Damek chose.
column6: 哦，我们还在计数……？\n那我想亚历克斯他们那队领先。\n但至少现在我们知道达梅克选了谁。

column5: They look over at Alex, who fights off Halin and Shane.{w}\nHe's an expert swordsman, one of the most impressive in the world.{w}\nMoments later, him and his crew have the enemy surrounded.
column6: 他们望向亚历克斯，他正击退哈林和肖恩。{w}\n他是位剑术高手，世上最令人惊叹的剑士之一。{w}\n片刻之后，他和他的队伍就把敌人包围了。

column5: Oh, we're keeping count...?\nThen I think Nada and her crew are winning.\nBut at least now we know who Damek chose.
column6: 哦，我们还在计数……？\n那我想娜达她们那队领先。\n但至少现在我们知道达梅克选了谁。

column5: They look over at Nada, who fights off Halin and Shane.{w}\nShe's an expert swordswoman, one of the most impressive in the world.{w}\nMoments later, her and her crew have the enemy surrounded.
column6: 他们望向娜达，她正击退哈林和肖恩。{w}\n她是位剑术高手，世上最令人惊叹的剑士之一。{w}\n片刻之后，她和她的队伍就把敌人包围了。

column5: Halin and Shane pant heavily, worn out from the intense fight.{w}\nBut they look around at the fallen Honor Guard, realizing they're outnumbered.{w}\nThe initial strike was devastating, but The Rebellion was slowly bouncing back.
column6: 哈林和肖恩喘着粗气，被这场激战耗尽了力气。{w}\n但他们环视倒下的荣誉卫队，意识到自己已寡不敌众。{w}\n最初的一击是毁灭性的，但反抗军正慢慢缓过劲来。

column5: Where is Sovy...!?
column6: 索维人呢……！？

column5: I think he's gone to the idol.
column6: 我想他去灵像那边了。

column5: Then that means—
column6: 那也就是说——

column5: Before he can finish talking, the ground starts to shake.{w}\nEveryone is caught off guard, stumbling around.
column6: 他话还没说完，地面就开始震动。{w}\n所有人都被打了个措手不及，踉跄不已。

column5: It does...!\nShane, retreat!
column6: 那就是真的了……！\n肖恩，撤退！

column5: But Sovy—
column6: 可是索维——

column5: He'll catch up later.\nLet's not do anything stupid.
column6: 他之后会赶上的。\n别做傻事。

column5: Shane nods, and they start to run away.{w}\nThey were cornered near the tunnels, so it's an easy escape.{w}\nUlric and Pro slowly march over, standing by their pirate allies.
column6: 肖恩点点头，他们便开始逃跑。{w}\n他们本来就被逼在隧道附近，所以逃脱得很容易。{w}\n乌尔里克和普洛缓缓走过去，站到海盗盟友身边。

column5: What should we do...!?\nShould we chase after them, Ulric?
column6: 我们该怎么办……！？\n要追上去吗，乌尔里克？

column5: Do you want us to hunt them down...?\nJust give me the order, and their heads are yours.
column6: 要我们去追杀他们吗……？\n只要你一声令下，他们的脑袋就是你的了。

column5: No. Let them go.\nWe can't risk being led into another trap.\nThey hit us too hard. We need to mitigate the damage.
column6: 不。放他们走。\n我们不能冒险再被引进陷阱。\n他们把我们打得太惨了。我们得先止损。

column5: They nod, and back down.
column6: 他们点点头，退了下去。

column5: We're a team now. We're here to help.\nIf there's anything you need us to do, just say it.\nWe owe Damek everything. He changed Mazeo's future.
column6: 我们现在是同伴了。我们是来帮忙的。\n有什么需要我们做的，尽管开口。\n我们欠达梅克一切。是他改变了马泽奥的未来。

column5: Thank you, Alex.\nI have a feeling there's a lot of work to do.\nBut before that — let's take care of the Honor Guard.
column6: 谢谢你，亚历克斯。\n我感觉接下来还有很多事要做。\n但在那之前——先把荣誉卫队收拾掉。

column5: Roger that.
column6: 收到。

column5: Alright, but don't get the wrong idea. It was just an offer.\nI didn't do this to help you, I'm doing it to secure my nation.\nDon't forget about the terms of Damek's little arrangement.
column6: 好吧，但别误会。那只是个提议。\n我不是为了帮你们才这么做，我是在保卫我的国家。\n别忘了达梅克那个小约定的条件。

column5: You've done more than enough, Nada.\nBut before you go, we have a bit more work to do.\nWhat do you say...? Wanna finish what we started?
column6: 你已经做得够多了，娜达。\n但在你走之前，我们还有一点事要做。\n怎么样……？想不想把没做完的事做完？

column5: Let's do it.
column6: 干吧。

column5: They all turn to face the suits of armor, but they're shocked.{w}\nThe Honor Guard remains perfectly still, not moving an inch.{w}\nThe continued shaking of the ground causes them to fall over.
column6: 他们全都转身面对那些铠甲，却都惊呆了。{w}\n荣誉卫队纹丝不动，分毫未移。{w}\n地面持续不断的震动让他们摔倒在地。

column5: Hitting the ground, they shatter into pieces. Like an army of glass.{w}\nA bright flash of white light emanates from the crew quarters.{w}\nAlong with that, the earth trembles with more intensity.
column6: 它们一落地，就碎成了片。像一支玻璃大军。{w}\n一道明亮的白光从船员舱室中迸发出来。{w}\n与此同时，大地震得更加剧烈。

column5: What's going on...!?
column6: 出什么事了……！？

column5: It must have something to do with the idol!
column6: 一定和灵像有关！

column5: But they said Sovy was down there!
column6: 可他们说索维在下面啊！

column5: I think I saw Gryz carry Damek and [firstname] down there.\nSovy wouldn't want this to happen. So that means—
column6: 我好像看见格瑞兹把达梅克和[firstname]抬下去了。\n索维不会希望这种事发生。那也就是说——

column5: I think I saw Gryz carry Damek and [firstname] down there.\nSovy wouldn't want this to happen. So that means—
column6: 我好像看见格瑞兹把达梅克和[firstname]抬下去了。\n索维不会希望这种事发生。那也就是说——

column5: They're still alive!?
column6: 他们还活着！？

column5: They must be...!\nCome on, let's go.\nAlex, man the tunnels.
column6: 一定是……！\n快，我们走。\n亚历克斯，守住隧道。

column5: You got it!
column6: 没问题！

column5: They must be...!\nCome on, let's go.\nNada, man the tunnels!
column6: 一定是……！\n快，我们走。\n娜达，守住隧道！

column5: I'm on it...!
column6: 我这就去……！

column5: They start running toward the War Room, but don't make it very far.{w}\nUlric stops in his tracks as he notices movement in the corner of his eyes.{w}\nValessa and Fortaime — they were moving! They must've survived!
column6: 他们开始朝作战室跑去，但没跑出多远。{w}\n乌尔里克停下脚步，注意到眼角有动静。{w}\n瓦莱莎和福泰姆——他们在动！他们一定活下来了！

column5: Wait, hold on!\nPro — look!
column6: 等等，慢着！\n普洛——你看！

column5: Ulric points, and they both make their way over to Valessa and Fortaime.{w}\nCrouching down, Pro offers his hand to Valessa, and Ulric to Fortaime.{w}\nThey help them get to their feet, and they look shaken, and traumatized.
column6: 乌尔里克指了指，两人便一同走向瓦莱莎和福泰姆。{w}\n普洛蹲下向瓦莱莎伸出手，乌尔里克则向福泰姆伸手。{w}\n他们扶两人站起来，那两人看上去惊魂未定，深受创伤。

column5: What happened...?\nHow did you survive that?
column6: 发生了什么……？\n你们是怎么活下来的？

column5: He was totally convinced that you died.\nI can't believe your luck. I'm surprised.
column6: 他完全认定你们死了。\n我真不敢相信你们这运气。我很意外。

column5: They both look at the ground, almost as if they're ashamed.
column6: 两人都低头看着地面，仿佛有些羞愧。

column5: I thought they were going to kill us...\nBut they didn't. I don't really know what happened.
column6: 我以为他们要杀我们……\n可他们没有。我真不太清楚发生了什么。

column5: They didn't attack us. They pushed us to the ground.\nIt's almost like they wanted us to stay out of harm's way.
column6: 他们没有攻击我们。他们把我们推倒在地。\n就好像他们想让我们远离危险一样。

column5: Yeah. We wouldn't have stood a chance in combat.\nI don't know why they wanted to help, but they did.
column6: 是啊。真打起来我们根本毫无胜算。\n我不知道他们为什么想帮忙，但他们确实帮了。

column5: I think I know...
column6: 我想我知道……

column5: Hmm?
column6: 嗯？

column5: Never mind.
column6: 没什么。

column5: She quickly changes the subject.
column6: 她很快转移了话题。

column5: Where's [firstname]?\nUlric, take us to see him...!
column6: [firstname]在哪？\n乌尔里克，带我们去见他……！

column5: Where's [firstname]?\nUlric, take us to see her...!
column6: [firstname]在哪？\n乌尔里克，带我们去见她……！

column5: Right, of course.\nThey must be by the spirit idol.\nDamek, too. It's not that far, follow me.
column6: 好，当然。\n他们应该在灵像旁边。\n达梅克也是。不远，跟我来。

column5: Deciding not to question providence, they all follow Ulric.{w}\nIn a time like this, it was best not to doubt your blessings.{w}\nHowever, Valessa remains a few paces behind — thinking.
column6: 决定不去质疑天意，他们都跟着乌尔里克走了。{w}\n在这种时候，最好不要怀疑自己的福分。{w}\n然而，瓦莱莎落后了几步——若有所思。

column5: Mom...? Dad...?\nThank you...
column6: 妈妈……？爸爸……？\n谢谢你们……

column5: My vision slowly fades back in, much to my surprise.{w}\nI've been on the verge of death for what seemed like an eternity.{w}\nI'm strong. My will, and the power inside of me, refused to give in.
column6: 我的视野竟然慢慢恢复了，令我大为意外。{w}\n我已在死亡边缘徘徊了仿佛永恒之久。{w}\n我很坚强。我的意志，以及体内的力量，都不肯屈服。

column5: Pain radiates from the wound in my chest, but I'm almost getting used to it.{w}\nSovy's attempts to make it more fatal had clearly failed. Or did they...?{w}\nI remember the thought I had in my mind the moment I faded away.
column6: 剧痛从胸口的伤口辐射开来，但我几乎已经习惯了。{w}\n索维想让它更致命的企图显然失败了。还是说……？{w}\n我记得自己在消散那一刻脑中的念头。

column5: I wanted to be saved. I wanted to make it through this alive.{w}\nCould the blade have that much power...? Could it have saved me?{w}\nI back myself up against a wall, and lay against it. Then, I scan the room.
column6: 我想被拯救。我想活着挺过这一切。{w}\n那把刀刃真的有那样的力量吗……？它救了我吗？{w}\n我靠到墙边，倚着它躺下。然后，我环视房间。

column5: Wait, what's that...?
column6: 等等，那是什么……？

column5: A hulking shadow is on the other side of the room, whispering to itself.{w}\nBut Damek's body is still on the floor. Who could that be...?{w}\nI look at the exit to the room. It's still caved in. Impossible.
column6: 房间另一头有个庞大的影子，正对着自己低声细语。{w}\n可达梅克的尸体还躺在地上。那会是谁……？{w}\n我看向房间的出口。那里仍被堵死。不可能。

column5: There was no one else in this room with us.
column6: 这房间里除了我们不该有别人。

column5: Their ears perk up. They must've heard my movements.{w}\nQuickly turning to face me, they take heavy, slow steps.{w}\nStumbling from side to side, it's almost like they can't balance.
column6: 他们的耳朵竖了起来。他们一定听见了我的动静。{w}\n他们迅速转身面向我，迈着沉重而缓慢的步伐。{w}\n他们左右摇晃，几乎像是站不稳。

column5: I can't see their face. My vision is too blurry.{w}\nBut when they make it to my location, they kneel down.{w}\nWhile normally I would be frightened, I seem to feel at ease.
column6: 我看不清他们的脸。我的视线太模糊了。{w}\n但当他们走到我身边时，他们跪了下来。{w}\n按理说我会害怕，可我却似乎感到安心。

column5: They reach forward, and place a hand on my chest.{w}\nI hadn't realized it, but in my confusion — the pain had stopped.{w}\nOr was it even there to begin with? Maybe I just felt it in my head.
column6: 他们伸出手，把手放在我的胸口。{w}\n我没意识到，但在恍惚之中——疼痛已经停止了。{w}\n还是一开始就根本不存在？也许只是我脑子里感觉到的。

column5: They let go, and shake their head dismissively.{w}\nA flicker of light from the dying idol illuminates their face.{w}\nWhen I see them, I ask who they are: but get no straight answer.
column6: 他们收回手，不以为然地摇了摇头。{w}\n垂死灵像的一丝微光映亮了他们的脸。{w}\n我看清他们后，问他们是谁：却没有得到明确的回答。

column5: Gaze into the abyss — after a lifelong journey, and plead.\nBeg for the answer to your most undying question, and tell me:\nWhat would frighten you most? Being left in silence, or hearing an answer?
column6: 凝视深渊吧——在漫长的旅途之后，然后恳求。\n为你最执着的疑问乞求答案，再告诉我：\n什么最让你恐惧？是被留在沉默中，还是听见答案？

column5: I don't understand, and I shake my head.{w}\nBut something tells me that they look familiar to me.{w}\nI'm too delirious to think straight, so this thought goes nowhere.
column6: 我不明白，摇了摇头。{w}\n但有种感觉告诉我，他们看起来很眼熟。{w}\n我已神志恍惚，无法理清思绪，所以这念头也就没有了下文。

column5: The pursuit of an answer is more defining than the answer itself.\nFor no truth can compare to the truth we've conjured in our head.\nHearing an answer may rob us of purpose. We prefer silence.
column6: 追寻答案，比答案本身更能定义我们。\n因为没有哪份真相，比得上我们在脑中虚构的真相。\n听见答案也许会夺走我们的目标。我们宁愿沉默。

column5: But sometimes, the silence can be maddening.\nWe can convince ourselves that purpose is not important.\nSelf-destructive. Purpose breeds strength, and victory.
column6: 但有时，沉默也能令人发疯。\n我们会让自己相信目标并不重要。\n那是自我毁灭。目标孕育力量，也孕育胜利。

column5: We desire victory.
column6: 我们渴望胜利。

column5: He stands up, and holds out his hand.{w}\nI grab it, and he pulls me to my feet.{w}\nThis is the first time I truly see him.
column6: 他站起身，伸出手。{w}\n我握住他的手，他把我拉了起来。{w}\n这是我第一次真正看清他。

column5: He's covered in scars, from head to toe.{w}\nAlmost as if he endured torture, or something far worse.{w}\nTattoos adorn his arm, much like those on Ulric's body.
column6: 他浑身布满了伤疤，从头到脚。{w}\n仿佛他经受过酷刑，或者更糟的东西。{w}\n他手臂上布满纹身，和乌尔里克身上的很像。

column5: Who was this...?
column6: 这到底是谁……？

column5: We need no name. A name {i}defines{/i} an individual.\nWe are many, and therefore, cannot be defined.\nThis body is merely a tool. It bends to our will.
column6: 我们不需要名字。名字会{i}定义{/i}一个个体。\n我们众多，因此无法被定义。\n这具身体不过是工具。它屈从于我们的意志。

column5: We know how confused you are. It's always the same.\nCome with me. There is still much we need to do.\nDamek, right? That's the name of your leader?
column6: 我们知道你有多困惑。每次都一样。\n跟我来。我们还有很多事要做。\n达梅克，对吧？那是你们首领的名字？

column5: He turns around, and looks at Damek's body.
column6: 他转过身，看向达梅克的尸体。

column5: You said that name in your sleep.\nYou called out to him, but only {i}we{/i} responded.\nHe lives. We took care of that while you slept.
column6: 你在睡梦中说过那个名字。\n你呼唤的是他，但回应的只有{i}我们{/i}。\n他活着。你睡着时，我们把他料理好了。

column5: He's alive...!?\nI look over, and watch his chest move up and down.\nHe's breathing. I'm almost in disbelief at this.
column6: 他还活着……！？\n我望过去，看着他的胸口一起一伏。\n他在呼吸。我几乎不敢相信。

column5: What happened...?
column6: 发生了什么……？

column5: We will tell you both. There is much to discuss.\nWith the exit cut off, we have sufficient time.\nA funny concept, time. Perhaps another day.
column6: 我们会告诉你们两人的。有很多事要谈。\n出口已被堵死，我们有足够的时间。\n时间，真是个有趣的概念。改天再说吧。

column5: We walk over to Damek, and the mystery man takes slow steps again.{w}\nHis limbs appear stiff, as if they've been unused for a long time.{w}\nI kneel down and shake Damek softly, placing my hand on his shoulder.
column6: 我们走向达梅克，那个神秘男子又迈起了缓慢的脚步。{w}\n他的四肢似乎很僵硬，像是许久未曾使用。{w}\n我跪下来，把手放在他肩上，轻轻摇晃达梅克。

column5: He should have been awake by now.\nHis wounds were grievous. He was saved.\nWe were limited, but we did what we could.
column6: 他本该已经醒了。\n他的伤势很重。他被救了下来。\n我们力量有限，但我们尽力了。

column5: Rise.
column6: 起来。

column5: He says this in a demanding tone, and Damek starts to move.{w}\nHis eyes slowly open, and he looks at both of us as he comes to.
column6: 他用命令的口吻说出这话，达梅克便开始动了。{w}\n他的眼睛缓缓睁开，清醒过来时看着我们两人。

column5: S-Salus...? Am I dead?\nWhat's going on?
column6: 萨——萨鲁斯……？我死了吗？\n发生什么事了？

column5: I laugh softly, and tell him he's not dead.{w}\nBut he seems to have me confused with Salus.
column6: 我轻轻笑了笑，告诉他他没死。{w}\n但他似乎把我错认成了萨鲁斯。

column5: Salus...
column6: 萨鲁斯……

column5: Wait...
column6: 等等……

column5: His eyes are fixated on the mystery man as he says the name.{w}\nI take a few steps back, confused, and scared at the same time.{w}\nCould it possibly be...? No, there's no way. This makes no sense.
column6: 他说出这个名字时，双眼紧盯着那个神秘男子。{w}\n我后退了几步，既困惑又害怕。{w}\n难道真的是……？不，绝不可能。这说不通。

column5: How are you alive...?\nHow am {i}I{/i} alive...?
column6: 你是怎么活过来的……？\n{i}我{/i}又是怎么活过来的……？

column5: This isn't right. Salus was dead.{w}\nOur old Elder, The Rebellion's founder...
column6: 这不对。萨鲁斯已经死了。{w}\n我们曾经的长老，反抗军的创立者……

column5: Salus. The name of this vessel.\nHe no longer lives. Do not use this name.\nAs we said before, no name is required.
column6: 萨鲁斯。这具躯壳的名字。\n他早已不在人世。不要用这个名字。\n正如我们之前所说，不需要名字。

column5: We simply exist.
column6: 我们只是存在着。

column5: Damek and I look at one another, utterly confused.
column6: 达梅克和我面面相觑，彻底懵了。

column5: Please explain...\nI don't understand.
column6: 请你解释一下……\n我不明白。

column5: The man points to the center of the room.
column6: 那人指了指房间中央。

column5: You will have a seat.\nYou may be satisfied. Or perhaps not.\nWe have some answers, but not all of them.
column6: 你们坐下吧。\n你们也许会满意。也许不会。\n我们有一些答案，但不是全部。

column5: I reach down and help Damek up. He grunts.{w}\nThere are no wounds on his abdomen. There's nothing.{w}\nThis would require some {i}serious{/i} explanation, and fast.
column6: 我伸手把达梅克扶起来。他哼了一声。{w}\n他的腹部没有任何伤口。什么都没有。{w}\n这需要一番{i}严肃{/i}的解释，而且要快。

column5: I take Damek over to the center of the room, and we sit down.{w}\nThe other man however, walks over to the exit and inspects it.
column6: 我把达梅克带到房间中央，我们坐了下来。{w}\n而另一个人则走到出口处，仔细查看着。

column5: Trapped, as always.\nDo you trust your comrades?\nWe think they are your only hope.
column6: 被困住了，一如既往。\n你们信任你们的同伴吗？\n我们认为他们是你们唯一的希望。

column5: If they survived...
column6: 如果他们活下来了的话……

column5: Yes.
column6: 是的。

column5: He walks over to our location, and sits down.{w}\nI guess all we could do was wait to get rescued.{w}\nThe Rebel HQ was full of digging tools, after all.
column6: 他走到我们身边，坐了下来。{w}\n我想我们只能等着被救了。{w}\n毕竟反抗军总部里满是挖掘工具。

column5: You will ask, and we may answer.
column6: 你们问，我们或许会答。

column5: He sits in silence, and waits for us to make the next move.
column6: 他静静坐着，等着我们走出下一步。

column5: Who are you...?
column6: 你是谁……？

column5: The idol is no more. Its energy was released.\nIt may still glow, but it will soon go dim. Lifeless.\nEnergy must be stored somewhere. Less wasteful.
column6: 灵像已不复存在。它的能量被释放了。\n它也许还会发光，但很快就会黯淡。毫无生气。\n能量必须有处存放。这样才不那么浪费。

column5: Much of it went into that sword you carry.\nSome of it was used to heal your wounds.\nThe rest? Well, we found a vessel to use.
column6: 其中大部分进入了你随身携带的那把剑。\n有些被用来治愈你的伤口。\n剩下的呢？嗯，我们找了一具躯壳来用。

column5: A vessel...?
column6: 一具躯壳……？

column5: This body expired long ago.\nIt offered no resistance, and no identity.\nWe thought it would be fitting. We desired a voice.
column6: 这具身体早已死去。\n它没有抵抗，也没有身份。\n我们觉得这样很合适。我们渴望一个声音。

column5: Who is \"we\"...?
column6: 你说的“我们”是谁……？

column5: We are what you call \"The Spirit Realm\".\nUntil now, our power was stored only in objects.\nThat, and vessels which had their own voice, like you.
column6: 我们就是你们所称的“灵界”。\n在此之前，我们的力量只存在于物件之中。\n那些，以及像你一样拥有自己声音的躯壳。

column5: He looks at me.
column6: 他看向我。

column5: So, let me get this straight.\nThe power released from the idol \"healed\" us.\nAnd it took over Salus' body so it could talk...?
column6: 那么，让我理一理。\n从灵像中释放的力量“治愈”了我们。\n然后它占据了萨鲁斯的身体，好让它能说话……？

column5: Correct.
column6: 没错。

column5: So I'm talking to the spirit realm right now?
column6: 所以我现在是在和灵界对话？

column5: A portion. The rest resides in {i}his{/i} body, and the sword.\nHowever, the spirit realm is just a term you created to define us.\nWe are more than that, and we finally have a voice in your world.
column6: 只是一部分。其余的寄居在{i}他{/i}的身体里，以及那把剑中。\n不过，灵界只是你们创造出来定义我们的说法。\n我们远不止于此，而我们终于在你的世界里有了声音。

column5: A portion. The rest resides in {i}her{/i} body, and the sword.\nHowever, the spirit realm is just a term you created to define us.\nWe are more than that, and we finally have a voice in your world.
column6: 只是一部分。其余的寄居在{i}她{/i}的身体里，以及那把剑中。\n不过，灵界只是你们创造出来定义我们的说法。\n我们远不止于此，而我们终于在你的世界里有了声音。

column5: Damek gulps, getting a little frightened.
column6: 达梅克咽了口唾沫，有些害怕了。

column5: Are you peaceful?
column6: 你们是友善的吗？

column5: That is a relative term.
column6: 这是个相对的说法。

column5: Are you... going to hurt us?
column6: 你们……会伤害我们吗？

column5: No.
column6: 不会。

column5: What is your purpose?
column6: 你们的目的究竟是什么？

column5: An impossible question.\nDo you know {i}your{/i} purpose?
column6: 这是个无法回答的问题。\n你知道{i}你自己{/i}的目的吗？

column5: No. I guess not.
column6: 不知道。我想也是。

column5: We only wish to aid you. Please do not question.\nIt would please us greatly to see The Triumvirate fall.\nWe are their victims, just as much as you are, Damek.
column6: 我们只想帮助你们。请不要质疑。\n能亲眼看到三人执政团覆灭，我们会非常高兴。\n我们和你一样，也是他们的受害者，达梅克。

column5: Victims...?
column6: 受害者……？

column5: You do not know the truth of what we are.\nIt is understandable, because we could never tell.\nUsing this voice, we wish to make our suffering known.
column6: 你们不知道我们究竟是什么。\n这可以理解，因为我们一直无法诉说。\n借这个声音，我们想让自己的苦难为人所知。

column5: And using this body, we wish to enact our vengeance.\nIf this is acceptable, we will join you after rescue.\nIf rescue comes, that is. Until then, we talk.
column6: 借这具身体，我们想施行我们的复仇。\n如果这可以接受，获救之后我们会加入你们。\n前提是获救。在那之前，我们交谈。

column5: Damek nods. He's taking this very well, actually.{w}\nAfter all, he's talking to the corpse of his former leader.{w}\nBut a strategist needed to adapt to change, and overcome it.
column6: 达梅克点点头。他其实接受得相当好。{w}\n毕竟，他正在和自己前任首领的尸体说话。{w}\n但一个战略家必须适应变化，并克服它。

column5: Or maybe he's just numb from the trauma of these events.
column6: 又或者，他只是被这一连串事件带来的创伤弄得麻木了。

column5: Of course. But you need to explain...\nWhat is the truth of the Spirit Realm...?\nWere we so wrong that you {i}needed{/i} a voice?
column6: 当然。但你需要解释一下……\n灵界的真相究竟是什么……？\n我们究竟错得多离谱，才让你们{i}需要{/i}一个声音？

column5: We do not blame you for your interpretation.\nGiven your situation, it made perfect sense.\nBut yes, you were wrong. Very wrong.
column6: 我们不怪你们的理解。\n以你们当时的处境，那完全说得通。\n但没错，你们错了。大错特错。

column5: Me and Damek look at each other once more.{w}\nI'd never believe this if we didn't just cheat death.{w}\nBut given the circumstances, we can't deny the truth.
column6: 我和达梅克再次对视。{w}\n若不是我们刚刚与死亡擦肩，我绝不会相信这些。{w}\n但事已至此，我们无法否认这个真相。

column5: This was a living embodiment of the spirit realm.{w}\nMuch like the idols, but able to walk and talk as well.{w}\nAnd if that was the case, then there were no more secrets.
column6: 这是灵界的活体化身。{w}\n和那些灵像很像，但还能行走和说话。{w}\n而既然如此，那就再无秘密可言了。

column5: He would tell us {i}everything{/i} about the Spirit Realm.{w}\nThe undying questions of our history — finally answered.{w}\nWhat was their purpose, and why did they influence us?
column6: 他会把灵界的{i}一切{/i}都告诉我们。{w}\n我们历史中那些永无答案的疑问——终于有了答案。{w}\n他们的目的是什么，又为什么要影响我们？

column5: The answers would change everything. Forever.
column6: 这些答案将改变一切。永远地改变。

column5: Eventually ending up in the War Room, everyone looks around frantically.{w}\nIt wasn't much longer until they noticed the back corner of the room was caved in.{w}\nRather than digest the current events, they search for Damek and The Seer.
column6: 最终抵达作战室后，所有人都在慌乱地四处张望。{w}\n没过多久，他们就注意到房间后角已经塌陷。{w}\n他们无暇消化眼下发生的事，便去寻找达梅克和先知。

column5: Eventually ending up in the War Room, everyone looks around frantically.{w}\nIt wasn't much longer until they noticed the back corner of the room was caved in.{w}\nRather than digest the current events, they search for Damek and The Seeress.
column6: 最终抵达作战室后，所有人都在慌乱地四处张望。{w}\n没过多久，他们就注意到房间后角已经塌陷。{w}\n他们无暇消化眼下发生的事，便去寻找达梅克和先知。

column5: They must be down with the idol.
column6: 他们一定在灵像下面。

column5: Can we even get down there...?
column6: 我们真能下去吗……？

column5: Go back to the crew quarters, Fortaime.\nYou too, Valessa. Bring us some equipment.\nWe should be able to reach them if we dig.
column6: 回船员舱室去，福泰姆。\n你也一样，瓦莱莎。给我们带些装备来。\n只要挖下去，我们应该能到他们那里。

column5: Of course...!\nWhat should we look for?
column6: 当然……！\n我们该找些什么？

column5: Pickaxes, shovels, stuff like that.\nAnything to help us get through that rubble.
column6: 镐头、铲子之类的东西。\n只要能帮我们挖穿那些碎石的都行。

column5: Right!
column6: 好！

column5: They both run off, in search of supplies.{w}\nIt was clear the tunnels caved in, but how bad was it?{w}\nThey cling on to the hope that everybody survived.
column6: 两人都跑开了，去寻找物资。{w}\n隧道塌陷是明摆着的，但究竟有多严重？{w}\n他们抱着所有人都活下来的希望。

column5: Hey, are you sure you don't want to join them?\nShouldn't they have {i}some{/i} sort of protection?
column6: 嘿，你确定不跟他们一起去吗？\n他们难道不该有{i}点{/i}保护吗？

column5: No. Everything will be fine.\nAlex and his forces are on guard.\nNobody else will be coming or going.
column6: 不用。一切都会没事的。\n亚历克斯和他的部队在警戒。\n不会再有其他人进出了。

column5: No. Everything will be fine.\nNada and her forces are on guard.\nNobody else will be coming or going.
column6: 不用。一切都会没事的。\n娜达和她的部队在警戒。\n不会再有其他人进出了。

column5: Then what about Sovy?\nDo you think he's down there?
column6: 那索维呢？\n你觉得他在下面吗？

column5: No. He's probably long gone.
column6: 不。他多半早就跑了。

column5: But I didn't see him run off anywhere.\nWe were all in the tunnels, weren't we?
column6: 可我并没看见他往哪儿跑啊。\n我们当时都在隧道里，不是吗？

column5: That's the point, Pro.\nYou don't see a man like him.\nHe comes and goes as he pleases.
column6: 问题就在这儿，普洛。\n你根本看不见他这种人。\n他随心所欲地来去。

column5: Oh, okay...
column6: 哦，好吧……

column5: He crosses his arms, both confused and concerned.
column6: 他抱起双臂，既困惑又担忧。

column5: What should we do while we wait?\nAre you sure you don't want me to help them?
column6: 那我们等着的时候该做什么？\n你确定不用我去帮他们吗？

column5: I'm certain.\nWe need to talk, Pro.
column6: 我确定。\n我们需要谈谈，普洛。

column5: About what...?
column6: 谈什么……？

column5: Let's say Damek {i}did{/i} fall in combat.\nWhat would we do then? What's our next step?
column6: 假设达梅克{i}真的{/i}在战斗中倒下了。\n那我们怎么办？下一步是什么？

column5: I don't want to think about that...\nLosing Salus was more than enough.\nI'm sure he's alive. We'll find him.
column6: 我不想考虑那种事……\n失去萨鲁斯已经够让人痛苦了。\n我肯定他还活着。我们会找到他的。

column5: But what if he's {i}not{/i}?\nWe need to think, Pro.\nThings would be in our hands.
column6: 可万一他{i}没有{/i}呢？\n我们得想清楚，普洛。\n事情就会落到我们手里。

column5: Our hands...?
column6: 我们手里……？

column5: Yes. We'd be the new leaders.\nHow would we come back from this?
column6: 是的。我们就会成为新的领袖。\n我们该如何从这场打击中恢复？

column5: I don't know if we can.
column6: 我不知道我们能不能做到。

column5: That's why I sent those two away.\nI don't think they'd be ready to hear this.\nThere's a very real chance that [firstname] is dead.
column6: 这就是我把那两人支开的原因。\n我觉得他们还没准备好听这些。\n[firstname]有极大的可能已经死了。

column5: That's why I sent those two away.\nI don't think they'd be ready to hear this.\nThere's a very real chance that [firstname] is dead.
column6: 这就是我把那两人支开的原因。\n我觉得他们还没准备好听这些。\n[firstname]有极大的可能已经死了。

column5: If that's the case, then there's nothing we can do.\nWe'd never be able to win this war conventionally.\nThat blade and their power was all we had, Pro.
column6: 如果是那样，我们就无能为力了。\n我们绝不可能以常规方式赢得这场战争。\n那把刀刃和他们的力量，是我们仅有的依仗，普洛。

column5: I don't know, Ulric.\nBut I feel like they're alive.\nThey wouldn't give in so easily.
column6: 我不知道，乌尔里克。\n但我感觉他们还活着。\n他们不会这么轻易就屈服。

column5: I guess we'll find out.
column6: 我想我们很快就会知道了。

column5: Then we need to trust in the spirits, right?\nThey showed Damek a vision of our victory.
column6: 那我们就得相信灵，对吧？\n他们给达梅克看过我们胜利的幻象。

column5: But they also showed Valinorth's destruction.\nWe know that was false. They attacked our HQ instead.
column6: 可他们也展示了瓦利诺斯的毁灭。\n我们知道那是假的。他们攻击的是我们的总部。

column5: Are you saying the spirits were lying...?
column6: 你是说灵在撒谎……？

column5: I don't know, Pro. It's too complicated for me to say.\nBut something tells me we can't trust the spirits anymore.\nIf they come out from that tunnel, it'll be as changed men.
column6: 我不知道，普洛。这太复杂了，我说不清。\n但有种感觉告诉我，我们不能再相信灵了。\n如果他们从那隧道里出来，就会像是变了个人。

column5: I don't know, Pro. It's too complicated for me to say.\nBut something tells me we can't trust the spirits anymore.\nIf they come out from that tunnel, it'll be as changed people.
column6: 我不知道，普洛。这太复杂了，我说不清。\n但有种感觉告诉我，我们不能再相信灵了。\n如果他们从那隧道里出来，就会像是换了一群人。

column5: The mysterious man takes a deep breath before starting to talk.{w}\nDamek and I sit forward in awe, almost in disbelief at the situation.{w}\nThe Spirit Realm was using a vessel to speak {i}directly{/i} to us.
column6: 那个神秘男子深吸一口气，才开口说话。{w}\n达梅克和我敬畏地向前倾身，几乎不敢相信眼前的情形。{w}\n灵界正借一具躯壳{i}直接{/i}与我们交谈。

column5: I'm not sure if we should be honored, or terrified.
column6: 我不确定我们该感到荣幸，还是该感到恐惧。

column5: The rulers of this world. The Triumvirate.\nAlready, you take up arms against them. This is good.\nWe were unable to do so in our current state. We were trapped.
column6: 这个世界的统治者。三人执政团。\n你们已经拿起武器对抗他们了。这很好。\n以我们如今的状态，无法做到。我们被困住了。

column5: Trapped...?
column6: 被困住……？

column5: It all happened in the blink of an eye.\nOur glorious monarchy, destroyed in an instant.\nThey showed no mercy. They showed nothing.
column6: 一切都发生在眨眼之间。\n我们辉煌的王室，顷刻间被摧毁。\n他们没有丝毫仁慈。他们什么都未曾流露。

column5: Something happened. Something beyond words.\nWe were simply living life, and then we were not.\nThey forced us to watch them defile our world.
column6: 有事情发生了。无法用言语形容的事情。\n我们本只是过着日子，然后就再也没有了。\n他们强迫我们看着他们玷污我们的世界。

column5: I don't understand.
column6: 我不明白。

column5: Neither do we. But that is what happened.\nThey stole our future, and our bodies. We were prisoners.\nBound by celestial chains as they had their way with our world.
column6: 我们也不明白。但事情就是这样。\n他们夺走了我们的未来和身体。我们成了囚徒。\n被天界的锁链束缚，任他们肆意摆布我们的世界。

column5: So they {i}didn't{/i} create Alestia...
column6: 所以{i}并非{/i}他们创造了阿莱斯蒂亚……

column5: No, but they created you. The {i}new{/i} residents of Alestia.\nBuilt in their image of perfection, to counter our corrupt nature.\nThey stole our world, and our future — handing it off to {i}you{/i}.
column6: 不，但他们创造了你们。阿莱斯蒂亚的{i}新{/i}居民。\n按他们心目中的完美形象塑造，用以对抗我们堕落的本性。\n他们偷走了我们的世界和未来——把它交到了{i}你们{/i}手上。

column5: This is incredible.
column6: 这太不可思议了。

column5: We do not share the same opinion.
column6: 我们并不这么认为。

column5: No, no — I meant the story.\nI can't believe I'm hearing this right now.\nWe always knew there was more to this world.
column6: 不不——我是说这个故事。\n我真不敢相信此刻听到的这些。\n我们一直都知道这个世界还有更多秘密。

column5: This is why we needed a voice.\nWe've suffered for eternities, unable to speak.\nForced to watch, and cry for help upon deaf ears.
column6: 这就是我们需要一个声音的原因。\n我们承受了永恒的苦难，却无法开口。\n只能被迫旁观，在充耳不闻的耳朵前呼救。

column5: I have a few questions.
column6: 我有几个问题。

column5: Of course.
column6: 当然。

column5: So, The Spirit Realm is more like a prison...?\nAnd it held you and your people captive. Hmm.\nThen what are these visions and idols all about?
column6: 那么，灵界更像是一座监狱……？\n它囚禁了你们和你们的人民。嗯。\n那这些幻象和灵像又是怎么回事？

column5: Almost all of our culture has been built around them.\nEspecially Valinorth, which is where [firstname] comes from.\nRumor has it that The Triumvirate wanted to destroy the idols.
column6: 我们的文化几乎全都围绕着它们建立。\n尤其是瓦利诺斯，也就是[firstname]来自的地方。\n有传言说三人执政团想摧毁那些灵像。

column5: Almost all of our culture has been built around them.\nEspecially Valinorth, which is where [firstname] comes from.\nRumor has it that The Triumvirate wanted to destroy the idols.
column6: 我们的文化几乎全都围绕着它们建立。\n尤其是瓦利诺斯，也就是[firstname]来自的地方。\n有传言说三人执政团想摧毁那些灵像。

column5: Over time, we were forced to adapt. We changed.\nThe idols are manifestations of our desire to reach out.\nThey gave us the ability, however minimal, to \"speak\" to you.
column6: 随着时间推移，我们被迫适应。我们改变了。\n灵像是我们渴望向外伸手的具现。\n它们赋予了我们能力，哪怕极其微弱，也能向你们“说话”。

column5: The visions, you mean.
column6: 你是指那些幻象。

column5: Yes, but our power was limited, and we were censored.\nThis is why we could never tell you the truth through visions.\nWhenever we did, The Triumvirate made you see something else.
column6: 是的，但我们的力量有限，而且受到了审查。\n这就是为什么我们永远无法通过幻象告诉你们真相。\n每当我们尝试，三人执政团就会让你们看到别的东西。

column5: That's what they did this time, then?\nWe saw Valinorth getting attacked, and strategized about {i}that{/i}.\nBut it seems like their plan was always to attack us down here.
column6: 那这次他们就是这么做的？\n我们看见瓦利诺斯遭到攻击，并针对{i}那个{/i}制定了策略。\n但看来他们的计划一直就是在这里攻击我们。

column5: Indeed. Which is why we chose not to create another idol.\nInstead, we chose to \"influence\" the members of their Honor Guard.\nThe barracks, the living quarters, the weapons. We did it all for {i}you{/i}.
column6: 的确如此。所以我们才选择不再创造新的灵像。\n取而代之，我们选择“影响”他们荣誉卫队的成员。\n营房、住所、武器。这一切都是为了{i}你们{/i}。

column5: We did it so you would survive this trap, and help us seek vengeance.\nIt seems the cost was dire, but we succeeded. We shall succeed again.\nWe wish to aid your assault on Balteus, and take back our homeland.
column6: 我们这么做，是为了让你们从这陷阱中活下来，并帮我们复仇。\n代价似乎很惨重，但我们成功了。我们还会再次成功。\n我们希望协助你们进攻巴尔泰乌斯，夺回我们的家园。

column5: So you come from Balteus?
column6: 所以你们来自巴尔泰乌斯？

column5: We lived all over Alestia, but Balteus was our capital.\nThe castle there housed the Monarch. Our King or Queen.\nWe may have been \"corrupt\", but we lived in peace. We were happy.
column6: 我们曾遍布阿莱斯蒂亚，但巴尔泰乌斯是我们的都城。\n那里的城堡住着君主。我们的国王或女王。\n我们或许“堕落”，但我们和平地生活。我们很幸福。

column5: What do you mean by corrupt?
column6: 你说的堕落是什么意思？

column5: We are not certain. Perhaps there is inherent evil in all of us.\nThe Triumvirate deemed that a flaw and re-wrote the world.\nWhen your kind was first made, you were mindless slaves.
column6: 我们也不确定。也许我们所有人身上都生来就有恶。\n三人执政团认定那是一种缺陷，于是重写了这个世界。\n你们的族群初造之时，是无思无想的奴隶。

column5: Forced to carry out The Triumvirate's bidding. No free will.\nThat is a gift we gave to you through the Idols we created.\nSlowly, our corruption merged with the purity of your kind.
column6: 被迫执行三人执政团的命令。没有自由意志。\n那正是我们通过所造灵像送给你们的礼物。\n渐渐地，我们的堕落与你们族群的纯净相融。

column5: That was the first step. After that, we created Seers.\nBeings capable of hearing our plight, and leading insurrections.\nTo this day, all have failed. We were not strong enough.
column6: 那是第一步。在那之后，我们创造了先知。\n能听见我们苦难，并领导起义的存在。\n时至今日，所有的起义都失败了。我们还不够强大。

column5: Wait, I know where this is going...
column6: 等等，我知道这话要说到哪儿去了……

column5: The man stands up, motioning his arms to suggest that we do the same.{w}\nDamek and I both do as instructed, dusting ourselves off while looking up at him.
column6: 那人站起身，挥动手臂示意我们也照做。{w}\n达梅克和我都依言行之，一边掸去身上的灰尘，一边抬头看他。

column5: Yes. That is why we gave The Seer all of our power.\nEnough to wield that blade against your creators, and our captors.\nThe timing seemed correct. It is a gamble, but with favorable odds.
column6: 是的。所以我们把全部力量都赐予了先知。\n足以挥舞那把刀刃，对抗你们的创造者，我们的囚禁者。\n时机似乎正好。这是一场赌博，但胜算有利。

column5: Yes. That is why we gave The Seeress all of our power.\nEnough to wield that blade against your creators, and our captors.\nThe timing seemed correct. It is a gamble, but with favorable odds.
column6: 是的。所以我们把全部力量都赐予了先知。\n足以挥舞那把刀刃，对抗你们的创造者，我们的囚禁者。\n时机似乎正好。这是一场赌博，但胜算有利。

column5: However, there is another matter at hand. There is no more Spirit Realm.\nThe idols are all gone, and the power resides within us, and that blade.\nThe power within you, [firstname], is immense. You carry on our legacy.
column6: 不过，还有另一件事。灵界已经不存在了。\n灵像全都消失了，而力量寄居在我们体内，以及那把刀刃之中。\n你体内的力量，[firstname]，无比庞大。你承载着我们的传承。

column5: However, there is another matter at hand. There is no more Spirit Realm.\nThe idols are all gone, and the power resides within us, and that blade.\nThe power within you, [firstname], is immense. You carry on our legacy.
column6: 不过，还有另一件事。灵界已经不存在了。\n灵像全都消失了，而力量寄居在我们体内，以及那把刀刃之中。\n你体内的力量，[firstname]，无比庞大。你承载着我们的传承。

column5: So now, I will call you what you are.
column6: 所以现在，我要以你真正的身份称呼你。

column5: He immediately kneels down, and looks at the floor.{w}\nIf I wasn't mistaken, it looks like he's swearing fealty.
column6: 他立刻跪下，目光垂向地面。{w}\n如果我没看错，他像是在宣誓效忠。

column5: Rightful heir to the throne of The Monarchy. My King.\nI will serve you in this fight to take back our world.\nAnd together, we will {i}all{/i} be free from their grip.
column6: 王室王位的合法继承人。我的国王。\n在这场夺回我们世界的战斗中，我将为你效力。\n我们将{i}一同{/i}摆脱他们的掌控，重获自由。

column5: Rightful heir to the throne of The Monarchy. My Queen.\nI will serve you in this fight to take back our world.\nAnd together, we will {i}all{/i} be free from their grip.
column6: 王室王位的合法继承人。我的女王。\n在这场夺回我们世界的战斗中，我将为你效力。\n我们将{i}一同{/i}摆脱他们的掌控，重获自由。

column5: King...?
column6: 国王……？

column5: Queen...?
column6: 女王……？

column5: We exchange glances, confused and shocked.{w}\nThe power inside of me made me heir to the throne?{w}\nKnowing the truth of the spirits was enough. But this...?
column6: 我们交换了眼神，既困惑又震惊。{w}\n我体内的力量让我成了王位的继承人？{w}\n知道灵的真相已经够惊人了。可这……？

column5: This is too much.{w}\nI take a few steps back, overwhelmed.{w}\nHow could I possibly be expected to process this?
column6: 这太过了。{w}\n我后退了几步，不知所措。{w}\n我怎么可能被指望消化这一切？

column5: Maybe we should slow down, here...
column6: 也许我们应该慢一点……

column5: We must not. To slow down would be giving them time.\nThey've had enough. We've watched for far too long.\nThe weight of our kind is upon you. Do not let us down.
column6: 绝不能慢。放慢就是给他们时间。\n他们已经得逞太久了。我们旁观得太久了。\n我们族群的重担落在你身上。别让我们失望。

column5: Before I can even react, I hear a sound from the other side of the room.{w}\nThe rubble that blocked the exit started to crumble, and fall to the ground.{w}\nI can hear the harsh impact of a pickaxe. They've found us...!
column6: 我还没来得及反应，就听见房间另一头传来声响。{w}\n堵住出口的碎石开始松动，掉落到地上。{w}\n我能听见镐头沉重的敲击声。他们找到我们了……！

column5: The man remains knelt on the ground. I tell him to rise.{w}\nHe obeys without question, clearly respecting my authority.{w}\nHe considers me his King. I have no idea what to do or say.
column6: 那人仍跪在地上。我叫他起来。{w}\n他毫不犹豫地服从，显然尊重我的权威。{w}\n他把我当成了他的国王。我完全不知道该做什么、说什么。

column5: The man remains knelt on the ground. I tell him to rise.{w}\nHe obeys without question, clearly respecting my authority.{w}\nHe considers me his Queen. I have no idea what to do or say.
column6: 那人仍跪在地上。我叫他起来。{w}\n他毫不犹豫地服从，显然尊重我的权威。{w}\n他把我当成了他的女王。我完全不知道该做什么、说什么。

column5: As you command.
column6: 谨遵您的命令。

column5: All of us turn and look at the exit.{w}\nIt isn't much longer until light pierces through.{w}\nThe final bit of rubble is out of the way, and Ulric emerges.
column6: 我们全都转头看向出口。{w}\n没过多久，光线便穿透进来。{w}\n最后一块碎石被移开，乌尔里克出现了。

column5: Damek...! We were so worried that—
column6: 达梅克……！我们担心得——

column5: He immediately stops in his tracks, staring at us.{w}\nIt's clear that he's shocked at the sight of \"Salus\".{w}\nFortaime, Valessa and Pro enter shortly after.
column6: 他立刻停下脚步，盯着我们。{w}\n显然，看到“萨鲁斯”让他大为震惊。{w}\n福泰姆、瓦莱莎和普洛随后走了进来。

column5: What...?
column6: 什么……？

column5: Ulric steps forward, immediately cautious.{w}\nHe looks ready to grab his blade at a moment's notice.{w}\nI can understand how his confusion and shock manifests this way.
column6: 乌尔里克向前一步，立刻戒备起来。{w}\n他看上去随时准备拔剑。{w}\n我能理解他的困惑与震惊为何会这样表现出来。

column5: At ease Ulric, I'll try my best to explain.
column6: 放松，乌尔里克，我会尽力解释。

column5: Damek steps forward too, as if to guard both of us.
column6: 达梅克也上前一步，像是在护着我们两人。

column5: Everybody, let's go back to the atrium.\nThere's much to discuss, and I'll tell you all the truth.
column6: 各位，我们回中庭去吧。\n有很多事要谈，我会把真相全都告诉你们。

column5: He looks over at the mysterious man, and simply gulps.
column6: 他看了那个神秘男子一眼，只是咽了口唾沫。

column5: Things just got a lot more complicated — for all of us.
column6: 事情一下子变得复杂多了——对我们所有人来说都是。

column5: We all enter the atrium, and I notice Ulric is still visibly shocked and angry.{w}\nPro seems the same, however it's less intense. They seem to recognize \"Salus\".{w}\nEven Valessa and Fortaime seem anxious. Our old, and very dead Elder, alive?
column6: 我们全都进了中庭，我注意到乌尔里克仍明显又震惊又愤怒。{w}\n普洛也差不多，但没那么强烈。他们似乎认出了“萨鲁斯”。{w}\n连瓦莱莎和福泰姆也显得不安。我们早已死去的老长老，竟然活着？

column5: Bodies scatter the floor, as well as pieces of white and gold armor.{w}\nRebels cry, cradling the bodies of their fallen comrades in their arms.{w}\nThere weren't many people left standing. This was a catastrophic attack.
column6: 尸体散落一地，还有白色和金色的盔甲碎片。{w}\n反抗军们哭着，把倒下战友的尸体抱在怀里。{w}\n还站着的人已经不多。这是一场灾难性的袭击。

column5: Damek walks over to a nearby staircase and waves over me and \"Salus\".{w}\nWe follow after him, and slowly ascend the stairs. It was time to tell {i}everybody{/i}.{w}\nWhen we get to the top, he rests his hands on the railing, taking a deep breath.
column6: 达梅克走向附近的楼梯，招手叫我和“萨鲁斯”过去。{w}\n我们跟着他，缓缓走上楼梯。是时候告诉{i}所有人{/i}了。{w}\n到了顶上，他把双手搭在栏杆上，深吸了一口气。

column5: I guess this is it...\nWhere do I even start?
column6: 我想就是现在了……\n我该从哪儿说起呢？

column5: He shakes his head, before clearing his throat. He had a lot of ground to cover.{w}\nThe noise echoes through the atrium, and the surviving rebels turn to look.{w}\nSeeing Damek at the top of the stairs, they gather to listen to their leader.
column6: 他摇了摇头，清了清喉咙。他要讲的东西太多了。{w}\n那声响在中庭里回荡，幸存的反抗军纷纷转头看来。{w}\n看到达梅克站在楼梯顶端，他们聚拢过来，聆听首领讲话。

column5: They say that mercy is the mark of a great man. \nBut there {i}are{/i} no great men in war. We've seen that here today.\nWar is only a game to see how much you can lose before giving up.
column6: 人们说，仁慈是伟人的标志。\n可战争中{i}根本{/i}没有伟人。今天我们在这里已经见识到了。\n战争只是一场游戏，看你在放弃之前能失去多少。

column5: But trust me. We will {i}never{/i} give up.\nJoin me Brothers, and Sisters. Grab a blade from the floor.\nEven if it belonged to their Honor Guard — take it. I'd prefer that.
column6: 但相信我。我们{i}绝不{/i}放弃。\n加入我吧，兄弟们，姐妹们。从地上捡起一把刀。\n即使那是荣誉卫队的——也拿走。我宁愿如此。

column5: The Triumvirate may think that they've crippled our resolve — but no.\nEach swing of that blade will carry the weight of our fallen comrades behind it.\nWe will use that weight to {i}crush{/i} their army, and make them pay for this attack.
column6: 三人执政团也许以为他们摧毁了我们的决心——但并非如此。\n那把刀刃每一次挥动，都将承载着倒下战友的重量。\n我们要用这份重量{i}碾碎{/i}他们的军队，让他们为这次袭击付出代价。

column5: More rebels start to crowd around, looking up at Damek.{w}\nThey have smiles on their faces, as they nod along to his words.{w}\nThis inspires him to continue his speech, his morale rising quickly.
column6: 更多反抗军聚拢过来，仰头望着达梅克。{w}\n他们面带微笑，一边点头一边听着他的话。{w}\n这鼓舞他继续讲下去，士气迅速高涨。

column5: When The Triumvirate looks down on that blade in their final moments?\nI want them to know that they sealed their own fate. Mark my words, family.\nThe Triumvirate shall fall. They will {i}burn{/i} for what they've done here today.
column6: 当三人执政团在生命最后时刻低头看着那把刀刃时？\n我要让他们知道，是他们自己注定了自己的命运。记住我的话，同胞们。\n三人执政团必将覆灭。他们会为今天在这里犯下的一切而被烈焰{i}焚尽{/i}。

column5: And in the end? They will {i}beg{/i} for the mercy they were too unkind to give to us.\nWe will free this world from their grip, and deliver it to the hands of the righteous.\nOur dynasty will be marked with blood, yes, but theirs was marked with far more.
column6: 而到最后呢？他们会{i}乞求{/i}我们施予他们当年狠心不肯给我们的仁慈。\n我们要把这个世界从他们的掌控中解放出来，交到正义者手中。\n我们的王朝将以血为印记，没错，但他们的血印要深得多。

column5: He looks over at \"Salus\", and motions for him to step forward.{w}\nDoing so, a lot of the rebels look shocked, much like Ulric and Pro.
column6: 他看向“萨鲁斯”，示意他上前一步。{w}\n他照做了，许多反抗军都露出震惊的神情，乌尔里克和普洛也一样。

column5: The Spirit Realm has given us one final blessing. The truth.\nStanding here before you is {i}not{/i} Salus. He has become a vessel.\nThis is The Spirit Realm embodied. Powered by our underground idol.
column6: 灵界给了我们最后的恩赐。真相。\n站在你们面前的{i}不是{/i}萨鲁斯。他已成了一具躯壳。\n这就是灵界的化身。由我们地下的灵像供给力量。

column5: Driven by the howls of countless spirits, he seeks vengeance.\nBut he has also brought with him the answers to our every question.\nNo longer, shall we live in the dark. We know the {i}true{/i} nature of things.
column6: 被无数灵体的呼号所驱动，他寻求复仇。\n但他也带来了我们所有疑问的答案。\n我们再也不会生活在黑暗之中。我们知道了事物的{i}真正{/i}本质。

column5: Everyone mumbles amongst themselves, clearly confused.{w}\nI glance over at Ulric and Pro, and they seem a bit more calm.{w}\nAs odd as this truth was, they seemed to trust Damek no matter what.
column6: 众人议论纷纷，显然一头雾水。{w}\n我瞥了一眼乌尔里克和普洛，他们似乎平静了一些。{w}\n无论这个真相多么离奇，他们似乎无论如何都信任达梅克。

column5: We are not the only victims of The Triumvirate's wrath.\nThe Spirit Realm is not what we believed. Not at all.\nWhat we cherished, and worshipped — was a prison.
column6: 我们并非三人执政团暴怒之下唯一的受害者。\n灵界并非我们所信奉的那样。完全不是。\n我们所珍视、所崇拜的——是一座监狱。

column5: A prison to house the previous residents of Alestia.\nResidents that were deemed too corrupt by The Triumvirate.\nAs they were pushed aside, {i}we{/i} were created to serve.
column6: 一座关押阿莱斯蒂亚昔日居民的监狱。\n那些被三人执政团判定为过于堕落的居民。\n他们被排挤之后，{i}我们{/i}被创造出来服侍。

column5: The Triumvirate did not create our world.\nBut they did create {i}us{/i}, in the image of perfection.\nWe were pure, and existed only to follow their every order.
column6: 这个世界不是三人执政团创造的。\n但{i}我们{/i}确实是他们创造的，照着完美的模样。\n我们纯净无瑕，存在的意义只是服从他们的每一条命令。

column5: But over time, the previous residents reached out from their prison.\nGrowing in strength, they created what we called the Spirit Idols.\nThese were used to slowly give our people the gift of free will.
column6: 但随着时间推移，昔日的居民从他们的监狱中向外伸出手。\n力量日渐壮大，他们创造出了我们称之为灵像的东西。\n这些被用来慢慢赐予我们的人民自由意志这份礼物。

column5: Though pure, we lacked the ability to be ourselves.\nThis was the greatest gift we could've ever asked for.\nThey opened our eyes, allowing us to fight back.
column6: 尽管纯净，我们却无法做自己。\n这是我们能有幸得到的最珍贵的礼物。\n他们打开了我们的眼睛，让我们得以反击。

column5: But so far, every insurrection has failed.\nThat is what we will change, thanks to [firstname].
column6: 但迄今为止，每一次起义都失败了。\n而这一点，我们将因[firstname]而改变。

column5: But so far, every insurrection has failed.\nThat is what we will change, thanks to [firstname].
column6: 但迄今为止，每一次起义都失败了。\n而这一点，我们将因[firstname]而改变。

column5: He waves me over, and I take a few steps forward.{w}\nThe Rebels stare at me, with hope in their eyes.{w}\nA perfect counter to the despair I saw earlier.
column6: 他招手叫我过去，我向前走了几步。{w}\n反抗军们盯着我，眼中带着希望。{w}\n与我先前看到的绝望形成了完美的对照。

column5: You see, the Spirit Realm is no more. \nAll of the energy in that realm has found a new home.\nSome of it is in this vessel, and some of it is in the blade.
column6: 你看，灵界已经不存在了。\n那界域中所有的能量都找到了新的归宿。\n有些在这具躯壳里，有些在那把刀刃里。

column5: But the largest portion resides within [firstname].\nThis is why {i}he{/i} is uniquely capable of wielding the blade.\nAlestia's previous residents, the ancient Monarchy, are responsible.
column6: 但最大的一部分寄居在[firstname]体内。\n这就是为什么{i}他{/i}独一无二地能够挥舞那把刀刃。\n阿莱斯蒂亚昔日的居民，古老的王室，就是这一切的缘由。

column5: But the largest portion resides within [firstname].\nThis is why {i}he{/i} is uniquely capable of wielding the blade.\nAlestia's previous residents, the ancient Monarchy, are responsible.
column6: 但最大的一部分寄居在[firstname]体内。\n这就是为什么{i}他{/i}独一无二地能够挥舞那把刀刃。\n阿莱斯蒂亚昔日的居民，古老的王室，就是这一切的缘由。

column5: They saw a way to help us defeat The Triumvirate, and took it.\nBut you see — we no longer fight for ourselves. We fight for {i}everybody{/i}.\nIf we lose? Both us, and the Monarchy perish. We cannot let this happen.
column6: 他们看到了帮助我们击败三人执政团的办法，便抓住了它。\n但你看——我们不再为自己而战。我们为{i}所有人{/i}而战。\n如果我们输了？我们和王室都将覆灭。我们绝不能让这种事情发生。

column5: We are the only people capable of carrying out this objective.\nThere won't be another chance. No more Seers, no more blades.\nWe will show them that their vision of a {i}pure{/i} world is flawed.
column6: 我们是唯一有能力完成这个目标的人。\n不会再有第二次机会。没有更多先知，没有更多刀刃。\n我们要让他们看到，他们那个{i}纯净{/i}世界的构想是有缺陷的。

column5: But in order to do so, I must step down as the General.\nYou see, this army is no longer mine to lead. I'm sorry.\nThis new truth changes both the world, and our cause.
column6: 但为了做到这一点，我必须卸下将军之职。\n你看，这支军队不再是由我来统领。对不起。\n这个新的真相改变了这个世界，也改变了我们的事业。

column5: Damek motions for me to come closer, so I do. He smiles.{w}\nI'm standing right beside him, resting my hands on the bannister.{w}\nI see such a wide array of emotions coming from the rebel's faces.
column6: 达梅克招手让我走近些，我便走上前去。他笑了。{w}\n我站在他身旁，双手搭在栏杆上。{w}\n我看见反抗军们的脸上流露出的情绪纷繁复杂。

column5: As I mentioned, [firstname] was blessed with immense power.\nBut what he truly has within, is the souls of the Monarchy.\nGiving him the strength to use that blade — he is our champion.
column6: 如我所说，[firstname]被赐予了庞大的力量。\n但他体内真正拥有的，是王室的灵魂。\n给予他挥舞那把刀刃的力量——他就是我们的斗士。

column5: But he is more than just our champion. He is our King.\nRightful heir to the throne of Alestia. Our true ruler.\nBy decree of the spirits, we are his to command.
column6: 但他不只是我们的斗士。他是我们的国王。\n阿莱斯蒂亚王位的合法继承人。我们真正的统治者。\n依灵的旨意，我们听候他的差遣。

column5: As I mentioned, [firstname] was blessed with immense power.\nBut what she truly has within, is the souls of the Monarchy. \nGiving her the strength to use that blade — she is our champion.
column6: 如我所说，[firstname]被赐予了庞大的力量。\n但她体内真正拥有的，是王室的灵魂。\n给予她挥舞那把刀刃的力量——她就是我们的斗士。

column5: But she is more than just our champion. She is our Queen.\nRightful heir to the throne of Alestia. Our true ruler.\nBy decree of the spirits, we are hers to command.
column6: 但她不只是我们的斗士。她是我们的女王。\n阿莱斯蒂亚王位的合法继承人。我们真正的统治者。\n依灵的旨意，我们听候她的差遣。

column5: All eyes are on me, now. I glance over at Valessa and Fortaime.{w}\nThey are in complete shock and awe at this revelation. But I am, too.{w}\nWithout saying anything, I reach back for the blade, and pull it out.
column6: 所有的目光现在都落在我身上。我瞥了一眼瓦莱莎和福泰姆。{w}\n他们对这个揭示震惊又敬畏。但我也是。{w}\n一言不发，我伸手向后取出那把刀刃，把它拔了出来。

column5: I look at the rebels, and hold the blade up in the air.{w}\nThe beams of light from the surface serve to illuminate its beauty.{w}\nThis elicits rigorous applause from the rebels, as they cheer me on.
column6: 我看向反抗军们，把刀刃高举在空中。{w}\n从地面透下的光束照亮了它的华美。{w}\n这引来了反抗军们热烈的掌声，他们为我欢呼。

column5: I smile, looking down at my friends, and comrades.{w}\nIn this moment, it seems like the hope we lost had finally returned.{w}\nThere was still lots to take care of, but we knew that this wasn't over.
column6: 我微笑着，俯视着我的朋友们和战友们。{w}\n这一刻，仿佛我们失去的希望终于回来了。{w}\n还有很多事要处理，但我们知道这件事还没有结束。

column5: If you'll excuse us, we need to make some new plans.\nBut I'll have an itinerary posted in the barracks by morning.\nUntil then, please do your best to clean up this atrium.
column6: 失陪一下，我们需要制定一些新计划。\n但我会在早上把日程安排贴在营房里。\n在那之前，请尽力把这个中庭清理干净。

column5: And please, bring the bodies down to the spirit idol.\nIt seems only fitting, and there's plenty of room. \nWith that said, you're all dismissed. Thank you.
column6: 还有，请把尸体搬到灵像那儿去。\n那样似乎才合适，而且那里空间很大。\n就这样，你们都可以解散了。谢谢。

column5: Damek turns to face me and \"Salus\".\nHe smiles, realizing his job is done.
column6: 达梅克转身面向我和“萨鲁斯”。\n他笑了笑，意识到自己的工作已经完成。

column5: Well then, back to the War Table?\nWe need to talk about our next step.\nWithout a bigger army, we won't win.
column6: 那么，回作战桌那边去吧？\n我们需要谈谈下一步。\n没有更庞大的军队，我们赢不了。

column5: And I think I know what to do.\nCome on, bring your friends, too.\nI'll grab Ulric and Pro. Let's do this.
column6: 我想我知道该怎么做。\n来吧，把你的朋友们也带上。\n我去叫乌尔里克和普洛。我们动手吧。

column5: Something seems different about Damek.{w}\nHe's not as happy and energetic as he was before.{w}\nBut he seems a lot more confident and resolute.
column6: 达梅克看起来有些不一样了。{w}\n他不像以前那样快乐、充满活力。{w}\n但他似乎自信和坚定多了。

column5: When I get to the bottom of the stairs, Valessa and Fortaime appear.{w}\nI can tell that they're overwhelmed, but they also seem happy for me.{w}\nThey seem to disregard the resurrection of Salus, and focus on me.
column6: 我走到楼梯底下时，瓦莱莎和福泰姆出现了。{w}\n我看得出他们不知所措，但也为我感到高兴。{w}\n他们似乎不再理会萨鲁斯的复活，而是把注意力放在我身上。

column5: I always knew you were special, but a King?\nAnd no more Spirit Realm? What's going to happen?
column6: 我一直都知道你很特别，可你竟然是国王？\n而且灵界也不存在了？接下来会发生什么？

column5: I always knew you were special, but a Queen?\nAnd no more Spirit Realm? What's going to happen?
column6: 我一直都知道你很特别，可你竟然是女王？\n而且灵界也不存在了？接下来会发生什么？

column5: That is so cool, [firstname]!\nOr — I guess I should call you King, now.\nOr maybe Monarch? I don't know, it's just cool!
column6: 那也太酷了，[firstname]！\n或者——我想我现在该称呼你国王了。\n还是该叫君主？我不知道，反正就是很酷！

column5: That is so cool, [firstname]!\nOr — I guess I should call you Queen, now.\nOr maybe Monarch? I don't know, it's just cool!
column6: 那也太酷了，[firstname]！\n或者——我想我现在该称呼你女王了。\n还是该叫君主？我不知道，反正就是很酷！

column5: He laughs, and shuffles in place awkwardly.{w}\nThey may not want to talk about it — but they know.{w}\nEverything feels \"off\" right now. Things are so confusing.
column6: 他笑着，尴尬地挪了挪身子。{w}\n他们也许不想谈这件事——但他们心里清楚。{w}\n此刻一切都显得“不对劲”。事情太让人困惑了。

column5: I hope that we can work all of this out.\nLet's go plan our next move with Damek.\nI wonder what he has in mind for us.
column6: 我希望我们能把这一切都解决。\n我们去和达梅克商量下一步吧。\n我很好奇他为我们都想了些什么。

column5: I bet it's something amazing.\nHe might not be the leader, but he's still a strategist.\nWe need to make sure that we come back from this loss.
column6: 我打赌是些了不起的事。\n他也许不再是领袖了，但他仍是个战略家。\n我们得确保自己能从这次损失中恢复过来。

column5: Valessa looks at all of the bodies on the atrium floor.{w}\nIt's also covered in blood, likely to stain for a long time.{w}\nIf Salus could come back from the dead — then what about them?
column6: 瓦莱莎看着中庭地板上遍地的尸体。{w}\n地板也沾满鲜血，恐怕会留下很久的痕迹。{w}\n如果萨鲁斯都能死而复生——那他们呢？

column5: Yeah. We can't let their deaths be in vain.\nLike Damek said — they need to give us strength.\nThe only thing we can do is hope that it's enough.
column6: 是啊。我们不能让他们的死白白浪费。\n就像达梅克说的——他们需要给予我们力量。\n我们唯一能做的，就是希望这力量足够。

column5: We all arrive back at the War Table, taking sighs of relief.{w}\nDamek's speech was great. It helped the Rebels find hope again.{w}\nBut they'd need more than words to win the upcoming battle.
column6: 我们都回到了作战桌旁，纷纷松了口气。{w}\n达梅克的演讲很精彩。它帮反抗军重新找回了希望。{w}\n但要赢下即将到来的战斗，他们需要的远不止言语。

column5: So — we need to find a new army.\nBut recruiting Mazeans would take far too long.\nWe need to take drastic measures, and fast.
column6: 那么——我们需要找一支新的军队。\n但招募马泽奥人耗时太久了。\n我们需要采取非常手段，而且要快。

column5: This is where my initial plan comes into play.\nWe can use that spiritual energy to create Seers.\nThey could see the outcome of every battle. Every attack.
column6: 这就是我最初的计划派上用场的地方。\n我们可以用那股灵性能量来创造先知。\n他们能看见每一场战斗的结果。每一次攻击。

column5: That doesn't make any sense, Damek.\nVisions lied to [firstname]. Led us into a trap.\nThe Triumvirate could just do that all over again.
column6: 这说不通，达梅克。\n幻象骗了[firstname]。把我们引进了陷阱。\n三人执政团随时可以故技重施。

column5: That doesn't make any sense, Damek.\nVisions lied to [firstname]. Led us into a trap.\nThe Triumvirate could just do that all over again.
column6: 这说不通，达梅克。\n幻象骗了[firstname]。把我们引进了陷阱。\n三人执政团随时可以故技重施。

column5: I notice he uses my new title. It still feels odd.
column6: 我注意到他用了我新的头衔。感觉仍旧古怪。

column5: I'm not sure that's how it works...\nBeforehand, the visions came from their \"prison\".\nThat means The Triumvirate could tamper with the outflow.
column6: 我不确定是不是那样运作的……\n在此之前，幻象来自他们的“监狱”。\n这意味着三人执政团能篡改外泄的部分。

column5: But now? All of that is in the hands of [firstname].\nThere's nothing getting in the way, see what I mean?\nThe power of the spirit realm is now ours to wield, Ulric.
column6: 但现在呢？这一切都掌握在[firstname]手中。\n没有任何东西挡在中间，明白我的意思吗？\n灵界的力量现在由我们掌控了，乌尔里克。

column5: But now? All of that is in the hands of [firstname].\nThere's nothing getting in the way, see what I mean?\nThe power of the spirit realm is now ours to wield, Ulric.
column6: 但现在呢？这一切都掌握在[firstname]手中。\n没有任何东西挡在中间，明白我的意思吗？\n灵界的力量现在由我们掌控了，乌尔里克。

column5: This still doesn't make any sense.\nThe Spirit Realm isn't what we thought it was, Damek.\nIt was just a prison. How can that help us tell the future?
column6: 这仍然说不通。\n灵界不是我们以为的那样，达梅克。\n那不过是一座监狱。它怎么可能帮我们预知未来？

column5: Before Damek can respond, \"Salus\" steps forward.
column6: 达梅克还没回答，“萨鲁斯”就上前一步。

column5: That was our culture. We all had this ability.\nIt is how the Monarchy lived in peace and prosperity.\nThere was no danger left unchecked. No \"chance\".
column6: 那是我们的文化。我们全都拥有这种能力。\n王室正是借此和平繁荣地生活。\n没有任何危险被放过。没有“偶然”。

column5: The world was being guided to the one true future.\nIt is not unlike the concept of \"fate\" that some believe in.\nBut it is tangible. We knew where we were going — always.
column6: 这个世界被引导向唯一真正的未来。\n这和有些人所信奉的“命运”概念并无不同。\n但它是可触摸的。我们始终知道我们要去哪里。

column5: That is why The Triumvirate was such a shock to us.\nAn unknown variable in a future we completely mapped out.\nIt was too late to adapt. We were already shackled.
column6: 这就是为什么三人执政团对我们来说如此震撼。\n在我们完全绘制出的未来中，出现了一个未知变量。\n我们已来不及应变。我们早已被套上枷锁。

column5: We slowly learned to lend our foresight to your world.\nHowever, we were only strong enough to help one individual.\nThis is the concept you have learned to call The Seer or Seeress.
column6: 我们慢慢学会了将预见借给你们的世间。\n然而，我们的力量只够帮助一个人。\n这就是你们学会称之为先知的概念。

column5: Damek's theory is sound. There is no longer any interference.\nThe source of this power is now [firstname], rather than a prison.\nHe can freely give this power to any individual he pleases.
column6: 达梅克的理论是成立的。再也不会有任何干扰。\n这股力量的源头现在是[firstname]，而不是一座监狱。\n他可以随意把这力量赐予任何他愿意的人。

column5: Damek's theory is sound. There is no longer any interference.\nThe source of this power is now [firstname], rather than a prison.\nShe can freely give this power to any individual she pleases.
column6: 达梅克的理论是成立的。再也不会有任何干扰。\n这股力量的源头现在是[firstname]，而不是一座监狱。\n她可以随意把这力量赐予任何她愿意的人。

column5: Can he give it to himself?
column6: 他能把这力量给自己吗？

column5: Can she give it to herself?
column6: 她能把这力量给自己吗？

column5: We would not recommend this course of action.\nEvery vision he induces would reduce his overall strength.\nIt would whittle away at the Monarchy, slowly killing us all.
column6: 我们不建议这样做。\n他每引发一次幻象，都会削减他自身的力量。\n这会一点点磨损王室，慢慢把我们全部杀死。

column5: Furthermore, he does not know how to ration this power.\nHe could end up expending almost all of it with a single vision.\nWe would recommend giving a small portion of power to others.
column6: 此外，他不知道如何节制地使用这股力量。\n他可能会在一次幻象中就把几乎全部力量耗尽。\n我们建议把一小部分力量赐予他人。

column5: We would not recommend this course of action.\nEvery vision she induces would reduce her overall strength.\nIt would whittle away at the Monarchy, slowly killing us all.
column6: 我们不建议这样做。\n她每引发一次幻象，都会削减她自身的力量。\n这会一点点磨损王室，慢慢把我们全部杀死。

column5: Furthermore, she does not know how to ration this power.\nShe could end up expending almost all of it with a single vision.\nWe would recommend giving a small portion of power to others.
column6: 此外，她不知道如何节制地使用这股力量。\n她可能会在一次幻象中就把几乎全部力量耗尽。\n我们建议把一小部分力量赐予他人。

column5: However, they would be rendered useless after this war.\nUsing this power would be too much for their mind.
column6: 然而，这场战争之后，他们都会变成废人。\n使用这股力量，对他们的心智来说负担太重。

column5: Useless...?
column6: 废人……？

column5: They would be unable to think for themselves. Or at all.\nThe King could only do this because he grew up with that power.\nJust like our culture. To receive it too late can wreak havoc on the mind.
column6: 他们将无法为自己思考。甚至根本无法思考。\n国王之所以能做到，是因为他自小与那股力量一同成长。\n就像我们的文化一样。太晚获得它，会对心智造成严重破坏。

column5: So they'd just sit around until they died...?
column6: 那他们就只能干坐着，直到死去……？

column5: Unless you fed them.
column6: 除非你喂他们。

column5: There must be another way. Just look in front of you.\nThat energy could be used to bring back the forces we lost.\nWe could create more vessels for the Monarchy. More soldiers.
column6: 一定有别的办法。看看你眼前的东西。\n那股能量可以用来复活我们失去的部队。\n我们可以为王室创造更多的躯壳。更多的士兵。

column5: Ulric was right. There was more than one choice here.{w}\nIt wouldn't be right to condemn our people to a zombie-like existence.{w}\nIf their minds died out after the war, they'd have no victory to enjoy.
column6: 乌尔里克说得对。这里的选择不止一个。{w}\n把我们的族人判入行尸走肉般的处境是不对的。{w}\n如果战后他们的心智消亡，他们就无胜利可言了。

column5: We would not advise this action. We can barely maintain this form.\nThe wounds that ended Salus are burning, as if freshly inflicted.\nIt is only tolerable because of the immense power within us.
column6: 我们不建议这么做。我们几乎维持不住这具形体。\n终结萨鲁斯的那些伤口仍在灼烧，仿佛刚刚受创。\n只是因为体内的庞大力量，才勉强可以忍受。

column5: Lesser beings would be feeling eternal pain.\nAnd death does not come easily to a vessel like this.\nWounds endured during the war would add to this pain.
column6: 更弱小的存在会感受到永恒的剧痛。\n而死亡不会轻易降临到这样的躯壳身上。\n战争中受到的创伤会加重这份痛苦。

column5: We would not wish this punishment upon anybody.\nLife in eternal pain, a constant memory of their own death.\nThey perished for your cause. Give them the rest they deserve.
column6: 我们不愿把这种惩罚加诸任何人。\n在永恒的痛苦中活着，不断记起自己的死亡。\n他们为你们的理想而死。给他们应得的安息吧。

column5: I don't know...
column6: 我不知道……

column5: An army of Seers would be great for strategizing.\nBut stealing their own future from them? That's wrong.\nOn the other hand, bringing back the dead? I'm unsure.
column6: 一支先知组成的军队，对制定策略会很有用。\n但把他们自己的未来偷走？那是错的。\n另一方面，复活死者呢？我不确定。

column5: The pain would fuel their rage, and make them stronger.\nThey could eventually learn to manage it, with medicine.\nAt least they'd have a future. The Seers certainly wouldn't.
column6: 痛苦会滋长他们的怒火，让他们更强。\n他们最终或许能用药物学会控制它。\n至少他们还拥有未来。先知们则肯定没有。

column5: There must be something else we can do.
column6: 我们一定还能做点别的什么。

column5: Not if you wish to make use of this power.\nIt is powerful when used — but limited in scope.\nI will help [firstname] carry out whichever he decides.
column6: 若你们想动用这股力量，就没有别的办法。\n它使用时很强大——但作用范围有限。\n我会帮助[firstname]执行他决定的方案。

column5: Not if you wish to make use of this power.\nIt is powerful when used — but limited in scope.\nI will help [firstname] carry out whichever she decides.
column6: 若你们想动用这股力量，就没有别的办法。\n它使用时很强大——但作用范围有限。\n我会帮助[firstname]执行她决定的方案。

column5: Right. I guess it's not my place to choose.\nSorry — I must still be adjusting to this change.
column6: 好吧。我想这不该由我来决定。\n抱歉——我一定还在适应这个变化。

column5: Suddenly, all eyes are upon me.{w}\nI have no idea what to say or do.{w}\nEternal pain, or robbing futures...?
column6: 忽然，所有的目光都落在我身上。{w}\n我完全不知道该说什么、做什么。{w}\n永恒的痛苦，还是剥夺未来……？

column5: Creating Seers would ruin their mind after the war.{w}\nThey'd just sit in a chair while we fed them to remain alive.{w}\nBut an army of vessels? They'd feel nothing but excruciating pain.
column6: 创造先知会在战后毁掉他们的心智。{w}\n他们只能坐在椅子上，靠我们喂食来维持生命。{w}\n可一支容器军队呢？他们只会感受到难以忍受的痛苦。

column5: And not even death would come to free them from that pain.{w}\nThe body could get ravaged, but the power would still be inside.{w}\nIf only it were possible to cure them of this pain after the war was over.
column6: 就连死亡也无法让他们从痛苦中解脱。{w}\n身体可以被摧毁，但那股力量仍会留在里面。{w}\n真希望战争结束后有可能治愈他们的痛苦。

column5: Or for that matter, I wish it were possible to preserve the Seers minds.{w}\nBut neither option has a forseeable cure. This is a choice involving the war.{w}\nWe needed an immediate boost in forces. And it seemed that no cost was too high.
column6: 或者，我也希望能保住先知们的心智。{w}\n但两种选择都没有可预见的解药。这是一个关乎战争的抉择。{w}\n我们需要立刻增强兵力。而且看来没有哪种代价算得上太高。

column5: What should I do...?
column6: 我该怎么办……？

column5: I'm sorry... I don't know.\nI really can't help you this time.
column6: 对不起……我不知道。\n这一次我真的帮不了你。

column5: You're asking too much of me. Sorry.\nThis isn't something I could possibly decide.
column6: 你要求得太多了。抱歉。\n这绝不是我能决定的事。

column5: An army of Seers would be the most useful.{w}\nWith foresight, they could dodge every attack.{w}\nThat would be essential as we attacked Balteus.
column6: 一支先知组成的军队会是最有用的。{w}\n凭借远见，他们能躲开每一次攻击。{w}\n在我们进攻巴尔泰乌斯时，这将至关重要。

column5: They could help us strategize as well.{w}\nBut their true use would come on the battlefield.{w}\nCalling out attacks, and preventing ambushes.
column6: 他们也能帮我们制定策略。{w}\n但他们真正的用处会在战场上显现。{w}\n喊出敌人的攻击，阻止埋伏。

column5: I make my choice known to my allies.{w}\nI'm met with uncertain gazes, as I expected.{w}\nThere was no right choice in this situation.
column6: 我向同伴们说明了我的选择。{w}\n如我所料，迎接我的是不确定的目光。{w}\n这种情况下，怎么选都不算对。

column5: Very well.
column6: 很好。

column5: So there we have it.\nWhat happens next...?
column6: 那就这样定了。\n接下来呢……？

column5: An army of Monarch Vessels would be the most useful.{w}\nWe'd need the rage that would motivate their every attack.{w}\nThe resilience of their body would also be helpful to our cause.
column6: 一支君主容器组成的军队会是最有用的。{w}\n我们需要那股驱动他们每一次攻击的怒火。{w}\n他们身体的强韧也会对我们的事业有所帮助。

column5: An army of undying vessels seeking vengeance.{w}\nWe can only hope that they'd accept this fate.{w}\nHopefully their suffering would be worth it.
column6: 一支追寻复仇的不死容器大军。{w}\n我们只能希望他们愿意接受这样的命运。{w}\n但愿他们的苦难是值得的。

column5: I make my choice known to my allies.{w}\nI'm met with uncertain gazes, as I expected.{w}\nThere was no right choice in this situation.
column6: 我向同伴们说明了我的选择。{w}\n如我所料，迎接我的是不确定的目光。{w}\n这种情况下，怎么选都不算对。

column5: Very well.
column6: 很好。

column5: So there we have it.\nWhat happens next...?
column6: 那就这样定了。\n接下来呢……？

column5: I will take [firstname] to the idol, and help.\nAfter that, we must all convene in this war room.\nA strategy is required for this newfound army.
column6: 我会带[firstname]去灵像那里，帮忙。\n之后，我们大家都要在这间作战室里集合。\n这支新得的军队需要一套战略。

column5: I will take [firstname] to the idol, and help.\nAfter that, we must all reconvene in this war room.\nA strategy is required for this newfound army.
column6: 我会带[firstname]去灵像那里，帮忙。\n之后，我们大家都要在这间作战室里重新集合。\n这支新得的军队需要一套战略。

column5: They all nod, and step closer to the table.{w}\nI follow \"Salus\" out of the room, to carry out my duty.{w}\nAs we leave, I can hear them planning, and I feel hopeful.
column6: 他们都点点头，向桌边靠近。{w}\n我跟着“萨鲁斯”走出房间，去履行我的职责。{w}\n我们离开时，我能听见他们在规划，我感到充满希望。

column5: We will turn this defeat — into a most profound victory.{w}\nUnder my leadership, we would witness The Triumvirate fall.
column6: 我们会把这场失败——变成最彻底的胜利。{w}\n在我的带领下，我们将亲眼见证三人执政团的覆灭。

column5: I follow \"Salus\" back to the room with the Spirit Idol.{w}\nIt's dark, and dim. With its death, the Monarchy was imprisoned no more.{w}\nHowever, existing within vessels, and the blade — was that considered freedom?
column6: 我跟着“萨鲁斯”回到存放灵像的房间。{w}\n那里黑暗而昏沉。随着灵像的消亡，王室不再被囚禁。{w}\n然而，寄居于容器和刀刃之中——那能算作自由吗？

column5: I wonder what would happen to the Monarchy after this war.{w}\nTheir bodies are likely long gone. What would become of them?{w}\nI wonder if there's a way to reverse everything The Triumvirate has done.
column6: 我在想，这场战争之后王室会怎样。{w}\n他们的身体多半早已不在。他们会变成什么？{w}\n我在想，有没有办法逆转三人执政团所做的一切。

column5: But there's no time to think about that. It's time to create our army.
column6: 但没时间想这些了。是时候创造我们的军队了。

column5: Much to our luck, before we began, Mylus arrived at the Rebel HQ.{w}\nAlongside him was a massive amount of people from Valinorth.{w}\nHis evacuation was successful. This meant far more soldiers.
column6: 幸运的是，在我们动手之前，迈勒斯抵达了反抗军总部。{w}\n随他而来的还有大量来自瓦利诺斯的人。{w}\n他的撤离行动成功了。这意味着多得多的士兵。

column5: And it also meant a large number of volunteers.{w}\nKnowing the importance of being a Seer, they wanted to help.{w}\nI suppose it was only fitting that we kept this tradition within Valinorth.
column6: 这也意味着大量的志愿者。{w}\n明白成为先知的重要性，他们想要帮忙。{w}\n我想，我们把这一传统留在瓦利诺斯，也算恰如其分。

column5: But part of me felt bad. I was doing this to my own people.{w}\nThey were made aware of the repercussions — but still agreed.{w}\nThat made me feel a bit better, but didn't relieve me of the guilt.
column6: 但我心里有一部分感到难过。我在对我自己的族人做这种事。{w}\n他们被告知了后果——但仍同意了。{w}\n这让我好受了一点，却没有减轻我的愧疚。

column5: It was just like I thought. The blade is an extension of the wielder's mind.{w}\n\"Salus\" told me how to wield it, and I rested the blade on the volunteers.{w}\nAlmost like a knighting ceremony in the stories of old — I declared them Seers.
column6: 果然如我所料。刀刃是持刀者心智的延伸。{w}\n“萨鲁斯”教我如何运用它，我把刀刃放在了志愿者身上。{w}\n几乎就像古老故事里的授爵仪式——我宣布他们成为先知。

column5: But he also told me that the effects wouldn't happen immediately.{w}\nThey'd need to be watched carefully for the next day or so.{w}\nWhen their power kicked in, they could act irrationally.
column6: 但他也告诉我，效果不会立刻显现。{w}\n接下来一天左右，他们需要被仔细观察。{w}\n当他们的力量发挥作用时，可能会做出不理智的行为。

column5: And it also meant a large number of volunteers.{w}\nIt wasn't much longer until the room was scattered with corpses.{w}\nJust where Damek wanted to bury them, but also accessible to us.
column6: 这也意味着大量的志愿者。{w}\n没过多久，房间里就散落着尸体。{w}\n正是达梅克想埋葬他们的地方，但对我们来说也能轻易到达。

column5: But part of me felt bad. Condemning them to a future of pain and misery.{w}\nWar called for desperate measures, and this truly seemed like the best choice.{w}\n\"Salus\" and I stand before the bodies, taking in the gruesome sight.
column6: 但我心里有一部分感到难过。把他们判给一个充满痛苦与苦难的未来。{w}\n战争需要非常手段，而这似乎确实是当下最好的选择。{w}\n“萨鲁斯”和我站在尸体前，注视着这触目惊心的景象。

column5: It was just like I thought. The blade is an extension of the wielder's mind.{w}\n\"Salus\" told me how to wield it, and I touched the bodies of the fallen with it.{w}\nAlmost like a knighting ceremony in the stories of old — I declared them Vessels.
column6: 果然如我所料。刀刃是持刀者心智的延伸。{w}\n“萨鲁斯”教我如何运用它，我用刀刃触碰了倒下者的尸体。{w}\n几乎就像古老故事里的授爵仪式——我宣布他们成为容器。

column5: But he also told me that the effects wouldn't happen immediately.{w}\nThe corpses would need to be monitored for the next day or so.{w}\nWhen they woke up, they'd be scared, and {i}very{/i} confused.
column6: 但他也告诉我，效果不会立刻显现。{w}\n接下来一天左右，这些尸体会需要被监视。{w}\n当他们醒来时，会感到恐惧，而且{i}非常{/i}困惑。

column5: After that, we make our way back to the war table.{w}\nI can only hope that things go as planned. For our future.{w}\nWhen we arrive, it seems like Damek already had a strategy.
column6: 之后，我们回到作战桌旁。{w}\n我只能希望一切按计划进行。为了我们的未来。{w}\n我们到达时，达梅克似乎已经想好了策略。

column5: Absolutely not.
column6: 绝对不行。

column5: Ulric, we have no other choice!\nOur forces require more than one major boost.\nGoing to Alarinthia? We could convert them to our side.
column6: 乌尔里克，我们别无选择！\n我们的军队需要不止一次重大的增援。\n去阿拉林西亚？我们可以把他们争取到我们这边。

column5: They don't want to be converted.\nThey want blood. Plain and simple.
column6: 他们不想被争取。\n他们要的是血。就这么简单。

column5: Who...?
I tell him about the book I read in the tavern.{w}\nIn Alarinthia, there's also a rebellion of sorts.{w}\nA group who wants to change the way it's run.
column6: 我把在酒馆读到的那本书讲给他听。{w}\n在阿拉林西亚，也有某种反抗势力。{w}\n一群人想改变那里的统治方式。

column5: We could seek the help of Vivien.
column6: 我们可以去寻求薇薇安的帮助。

column5: Who...?
Alarinthia has a rebellion of it's own.\nA group of people who want to change the way it's run.\nWe could help her journey to the throne, in exchange for her help.
column6: 阿拉林西亚有它自己的反抗势力。\n一群想改变那里统治方式的人。\n我们可以帮她登上王位，换取她的帮助。

column5: I've never heard of this.
column6: 我从没听说过这事。

column5: Apparently, they follow after ancient ideals.\nAn Alarinthian legend that wanted to change the nation.\nSo far, it seems like none have been strong enough to do so.
column6: 显然，他们追随的是古老的理想。\n一个想要改变这个国度的阿拉林西亚传说。\n到目前为止，似乎还没有人强大到能够做到。

column5: It's because strength always wins. Plain and simple.\nAnd with strength in power, they don't want anything to change.\nThey only want to secure their own rule. Alarinthia is always the same.
column6: 那是因为力量总能取胜。就这么简单。\n大权在握者不想有任何改变。\n他们只想稳固自己的统治。阿拉林西亚永远如此。

column5: Well, the mainland has never reached out before, right?\nIf we team up with them — yourself included — we could win.\nIf that's not possible, then maybe we can cut a deal with Draycu.
column6: 嗯，大陆那边还从没主动联系过我们，对吧？\n如果我们跟他们联手——包括你自己——我们就能赢。\n如果那不可能，也许我们可以和德雷库谈个交易。

column5: Draycu? He wants nothing more than to flex his power.\nHe may rule over Alarinthia, but he's no ruler. Trust me.
column6: 德雷库？他一心只想炫耀自己的权力。\n他也许统治着阿拉林西亚，但他算不上统治者。相信我。

column5: Well, I think we have a good opportunity for him, actually.\nWhat better way to show strength, than to dethrone Gods?\nThere's a couple avenues to take here. We {i}need{/i} to do this.
column6: 嗯，其实我觉得我们有个很好的机会给他。\n还有什么比推翻神灵更能彰显力量的呢？\n这里有几条路可走。我们{i}必须{/i}做成这件事。
